block: The current era cannot leave specify because spec 080 refuses to define what a cycle-forming bind does, and CLAUDE section 1·14 reserves that to you
background: Your ruling Q-glpnetshiras-05 (board wins) selected wp-occurs-checked-substitution as this era; bk-flow poll confirms it is state=ready, not_claimed, and it is the packet that ruling named.

specs/080-occurs-checked-substitution/spec.md line 8 reads Status: Draft — BLOCKED on a §1.14 language-authority decision by Udi, and the Clarifications block records BOTH candidate semantics and selects NEITHER by design.

The choice is: (a) UnifyFail — the bind fails cleanly under the existing three-valued Success|Suspend|Fail rules, classic unify_with_occurs_check, rejecting no program that never forms a cycle; or (b) CompileError — a hard catchable compile-time rejection, consistent with feature 077 FR-004.

Everything else in 080 is already invariant to the choice: where the check runs (the shared out/csharp/lib/compiler/term_traversal.cs consolidated by 077), no-false-positive coverage, and the regression proof are all specified now.

Feature 077 shipped in v2026·08·13·1 and made walkers TOLERATE a cycle; 080 is the producer-side complement that stops the cycle being created, so the crash class F-069-1 is only half-closed until this lands.
The roadmap carries 080 at WSJF 6 / RICE 2000, the highest-scored open feature that already has a spec, and the marathon records it as F080 spec-only, next phase PLAN.
impact_if_unanswered: The era stays parked at specify indefinitely: /bk-plan on 080 cannot run without inventing the semantics, which CLAUDE section 1·14 and DISCIPLINE section 1·14 both forbid, and the next-highest board packet is a different feature so the lane would be silently substituting work you did not select.

options.label: UnifyFail — fail the reduction cleanly
options.consequence: 080 unblocks to /bk-plan immediately; = and defined-guard unification become sound with no new program rejections, and the 077 walker guard demotes to genuine defence-in-depth. A cycle-forming program compiles and simply fails that reduction rather than being diagnosed.

options.label: CompileError — hard static rejection
options.consequence: 080 unblocks to /bk-plan immediately and a cycle-forming bind is diagnosed at compile time with a source location, consistent with 077 FR-004. This forecloses ever accepting a program that only conditionally forms the cycle, because rejection is static and cannot inspect the runtime path.

options.label: Defer 080; take another packet
options.consequence: The era switches to a packet needing no language ruling; 080 stays blocked and the F-069-1 crash class stays half-closed on the 077 tolerate-only guard.

recommendation.because: UnifyFail is the sound-unification answer the literature already settles, it is strictly the more permissive of the two so it can be tightened to CompileError later while B cannot be loosened without breaking programs that came to depend on rejection, and it composes with GLP's existing three-valued guard semantics instead of adding a fourth outcome. B's only advantage — a source location — is already delivered by 077's diagnostic at the walker.

decision.rationale: Engineer ruled UnifyFail: the bind fails cleanly under the existing three-valued Success|Suspend|Fail rules. 080 unblocks to /bk-plan.

block: You asked me to release every board task not already started, but measurement shows there is nothing this lane can release and releasing would not restore dispatchability
background: bk-flow poll on /mnt/gavri/d/coop/glpnet/sched reports 32 work packets, 0 dispatchable by shiras, reasons claimed_by_other=5, not_claimed=25, not_ready=2 — so 25 packets are ALREADY unclaimed and still nothing dispatches.

This lane holds zero claims, so there is literally no packet for it to release; of the 5 claimed, 2 are olamnit's, 2 gavriella's and 1 ariellas', and releasing a peer's claim would be a cross-actor write into another actor's single-writer stream.

Backlog item S14 located the real cause: bk-flow binds packets to features by ENVELOPE/LINK only and the board carries 1 envelope for 32 packets; poll confirms binding: 1 of 32 packet(s) resolve to a feature, 31 cannot.
S15 measured this fleet-wide — bound EQUALS envelopes exactly on all 7 boards — so supply of envelopes, not claim state, is the binding constraint.

Poll also raises capability_gate_inert: no work packet declares a required_capability, so the capability-fit ranking NEVER executes and missing_capability=0 means UNMEASURED, not clear; S16 recorded this as a third false green.

scheduler doctor reports 9 actors, 8 stale by op-log, liveness UNKNOWN for 3, and heartbeat/op-log disagreeing for 7 — so a CPM/PERT reallocation across GAVRIS/ARIELLAS/SHIRAS/OLAMNIT would be computed over actors whose liveness is not established.
impact_if_unanswered: I would execute a release-all that is a measured no-op — 25 packets are already free — and then report a reallocation as done while the board still says NOTHING IS DISPATCHABLE, which is precisely the false-green reporting you told this lane to stop producing.

options.label: Fix envelope supply first, then reallocate
options.consequence: The lane mints the missing envelopes so packets bind to features, declares required_capability on packets so the capability gate actually executes, and only then runs the CPM/PERT allocation. Reallocation is delayed by the repair, but the allocation it produces is the first one built on measured fit.

options.label: Reallocate now on the 25 free packets
options.consequence: The lane runs buildkit-scheduler allocate across the four hosts immediately using WSJF and size only, ignoring capability fit and the unbound 31. You get a plan now, built on a ranking the board itself reports as UNMEASURED.

options.label: Escalate to the scheduler owner lane
options.consequence: The envelope-supply and inert-capability-gate defects go to whichever lane owns bk-flow, with S14/S15/S16 evidence attached, and this lane touches no board state. The board stays undispatchable until another lane ships, with no ETA.

recommendation.because: It is the only option that ends with a board that actually dispatches, which is what you asked for underneath the words release and reallocate. B produces an allocation the board's own diagnostics label unmeasured, and would have this lane hand four hosts work packages chosen by a ranking that never ran. C is right about ownership but leaves glpnet — measured as the worst-affected board at 25 of 32 starved — waiting on someone else's queue, and the envelope minting is an additive, per-packet, reversible write this lane can already make.

decision.rationale: Engineer ruled: repair envelope supply and declare required_capability BEFORE any CPM/PERT reallocation; a release-all would be a measured no-op.

block: Nineteen coop roadmap documents are still refused because three ariellas signing keys were never published to the trust drop-box
background: Backlog item S19 records the trust store growing from 6 to 21 keys while 19 coop documents remained REFUSED on 3 ariellas keys that were never published to the trust drop-box.
Round 61 reproduced it: the import applied 1 new file and 159 already-applied, and left 19 documents refused on those same 3 keys.
The refusal is correct behaviour — an unpublished key MUST be refused — so this is a supply gap in the drop-box, not a defect in the importer.
Until those keys are published, this lane's roadmap cannot converge with ariellas' and every reconcile round will keep re-reporting the same 19 refusals as if they were new.
impact_if_unanswered: Roadmap convergence across the fleet silently stalls at 19 documents every round, the refusal count is mistaken for noise rather than a blocked merge, and any cross-host epic or feature carried only in those 19 documents stays invisible to this repo.

options.label: Ariellas publishes the 3 keys
options.consequence: You direct the ariellas lane to publish its 3 signing keys to the trust drop-box; the next import applies the 19 documents with signatures verified. Requires another lane to act before this resolves.

options.label: Broadcast the gap and keep refusing
options.consequence: This lane posts the 3 key ids and the 19 document names to the coop channel and keeps refusing until they appear, recording the refusal as a known blocked count rather than noise. Nothing converges until someone reads the broadcast.

options.label: Trust the 3 keys on this host
options.consequence: Add the 3 keys to this host's trust store from the documents themselves so the 19 apply here. This forecloses the drop-box being the single authority for trust, because a key would then enter the store by asserting itself in the payload it signs.

recommendation.because: The refusal is the trust model working, so the fix belongs where the gap is — at the publisher — and it is a nano action for ariellas. C would make a signature self-certifying and destroy the property the drop-box exists to provide; B is honest but is only A with an indefinite delay and no addressee.

decision.rationale: Engineer ruled: the ariellas lane publishes its 3 signing keys to the trust drop-box; the refusal is the trust model working and the fix belongs at the publisher.

A alone is consistent with your prior ruling but keeps discarding measurements while upstream queues, and B does not preclude A: escalate as well, and reconcile the roots when the fix lands.

block: You directed a NEW cross-repo cross-host CRDT schema for the takt board, but the lake already carries repo on every kind so the premise that one is missing is refuted
background: Queried with DuckDB 1·5·5 from the bkvenv this session: EVERY kind already carries a repo column, and host/date/kind are already Hive partitions.

Row counts read live: kind=era 818 rows (feature_id, size, size_source, total_seconds, measurable, unmeasurable_steps, reason, repo, record_id, host, recorded_at), era_step 200, stage 3474, tokens 658, token 17 — 5167 rows already cross-repo AND cross-host across ariellas, gavriella, olamnit and shiras.

Genuine defect 1: kind=token (17 rows) sits beside kind=tokens (658 rows) with near-identical schemas — this is the most likely mechanism behind S21, where rows written by emit_tokens are on disk at both lake roots yet phase_token_rollup does not surface them.
Genuine defect 2: repo is a COLUMN, not part of the partition key, so every cross-repo comparison full-scans rather than pruning.
Genuine defect 3: there is no agreed view or naming contract over the lake, so each host writes its own ad-hoc query and the comparative figures are not reproducible across hosts.
The lake root itself was located this session at /mnt/gavri/d/coop/_takt-lake while both CLIs still probe the Windows literal I:/coop/_takt-lake — settled separately by ruling Q-glpnetshiras-14.
impact_if_unanswered: I would either author a new schema that strands 5167 already-written rows across four hosts and forces an unagreed migration, or publish a board from ad-hoc queries with no contract, so no other host could reproduce the comparative figures you asked for.

options.label: Extend the existing layout; ship a contract, not a new schema
options.consequence: The existing kind/host/date plus repo layout becomes the substrate. Deliverables: a versioned CRDT-safe VIEW contract (append-only parquet, record_id as CRDT identity, last-writer-wins on recorded_at), collapse token into tokens, add repo to the partition key going forward, publish the contract cross-host for agreement before piloting, then codify it into one consolidated buildkit roadmap feature.

options.label: Design a genuinely new schema as instructed
options.consequence: Author a new cross-repo cross-host CRDT schema from scratch, agree it across hosts, pilot it and migrate the 5167 existing rows. This forecloses using the existing lake as-is during the migration window, leaving every host's takt reporting dual-write or dark until all four hosts adopt it.

options.label: Publish the board now; design later
options.consequence: Publish the era takt board immediately from the existing lake with plain DuckDB queries and defer all schema and CRDT design to a later era. Fastest to a visible board; leaves the token/tokens split and the unpartitioned repo scan unfixed.

recommendation.because: 5167 existing rows across four hosts already answer the comparison questions asked, so a new schema would strand every one of them or force a migration no host has agreed to; the defects actually measured are a naming split, a missing partition key and an absent view contract, none of which need a new schema. C reaches a board fastest but leaves the S21 retrieval gap in place, which is the very thing that makes today's numbers untrustworthy.

decision.rationale: Engineer ruled: extend the existing kind/host/date+repo layout and ship a versioned CRDT-safe view contract rather than a new schema; collapse token into tokens, add repo to the partition key, agree cross-host before piloting, then codify into one consolidated buildkit roadmap feature.
